title: The Crying Trees
awards: Samsung KidsTime Author's Award — AFCC Singapore (2016)
blurb: The Crying Trees is a beautiful story about the Legend of rubber trees. Great Grandfather Tree showed love, courage and hope to save Father Tree, Mother Tree and all the little trees in Tree Land. Great Grandfather Tree sacrificed himself so all the trees could live forever.

title: Malong The Magic Cloth
awards: Best ASEAN Children's Book Illustration
Best in Fiction — International Children's Content Rights Fair, Chiang Mai, Thailand
blurb: What makes the Malong so special? Find out the mystery of the magic cloth as a little boy tells his true-to-life exceptional journey with his family. Children carry a little bit of enchantment all the time. This is the ultimate book for them to discover them magical this around them.

title: The Pencil Who Would Not Write
awards: First Prize — International Indie Children's Book Cover Award, Los Angeles (2021)
blurb: All the pencils love to write except for Ms. Yellow Pencil. She wants to stay sharp and tall, and keep her beautiful yellow skin forever. She thinks that if children will use her to write, she will become shorter until nothing is left of her but a piece of junk wood. So she ended up hiding herself under the stacks of Ms. Pad Paper inside a dark wooden shelf. Until something very terrible happened that she herself pleaded to be able to write again.

title: A Whale In Prison
awards: Best Children's Book — 18th Cardinal Sin Catholic Book Awards (2024)
Severino Reyes Medal Best Picture Book Honor List (2025)
blurb: Do you know that the biggest cause of harm and death of whales are when they get caught up in fishing nets and ropes? Around the world, hundreds of thousands of whales have been entangled to their death! This is true-to-life story conveys the message to children that we are all responsible for protecting the inhabitants of Earth - Our Home. As we do so, we are also protecting one another.

title: I Love Tnalak
awards: UNESCO–IBBY Remarkable Book for Young Readers in Indigenous and Endangered Languages (2026)
Launched at the 40th IBBY World Congress, Ottawa, Canada
blurb: Ngá Bun, a young T’boli girl, experiences emotions as varies as the patterns of the tnalak cloth. She discovers that the situations in life can spark in range of feelings, such as happiness fear, anger, relief, sadness and love. This story narrates how Ngá Bun navigates through her changing emotions. It also presents the hidden value of dreamweaver’s traditional handwoven cloth- the Tnalak.

title: Bulul
awards: Best Reads — 7th National Children's Book Awards (2020–2021)
blurb: When a pandemic hospitalizes her grandfather, Bugan takes up his place in the carver’s shed to continue the family trade of woodcarving. While this develops Bugan’s love for her roots, how will this prepare her for the news that is to come? This heartfelt story helps children and parents cope with the hardest challenge: The loss of a love one.

title: The Brave Little Stump
awards: Special Citation — Catholic Mass Media Awards (2025)
blurb: Read he story and find out about the courage of a Gmelina stump to persevere in the most tragic condition. A brave little stump stands fast. A brave little stump refuses to give up. A brave little stump holds on to hope for the environment and humanity.

title: Si Kamatis Inis
awards: Severino Reyes Medal Best Picture Book Honor List (2025)
blurb: Tomato grumbles about the insects that do not only crawl all over her, but also have made a home out of her leaves and stems. However, a visit from Butterfly and Bee makes Tomato realize that she and her new neighbors might be able to get along after all.

title: Barefoot Bulayan
awards: CNN Children's Books Best Reads
Shortlisted Best Reads — National Children's Book Awards (2021)
blurb: Children around the world belong to a particular culture. We need to encourage them to approach people’s differences by learning from one another, rather than judging or imposing on what we believe is right. Bulayan is a beautiful story that teaches children to respect different customs and beliefs. Yes, each person is different but no matter what, we are very much alike. Our hearts are the same. We all need to be loved and treated with understanding and kindness. A true-to-life story of a Bagobo boy who does not like to wear shoes.

title: Dearest Papa
awards: Best Children's Short Story — Catholic Mass Media Awards (2018)
Shortlisted Best Reads — National Children's Book Awards (2021)
blurb: War is a situation difficult for children to understand. Many children as young as four to five years old have written heartbreaking letters as their fathers and brothers go to war. These letters narrates their feelings, fears, hopes and dreams.

title: War Makes Me Sad!
awards: Best Short Story for Children — Catholic Mass Media Awards (2003)
2nd Place — AFCC Samsung KidsTime Author's Award, Singapore (2016)
blurb: An innocent child narrates her real life experience regarding the war between the Muslim and Christian people in Mindanao. She is appealing for peace and prayer. Reading the story could give each one a sense of the kind of pain a child is going through. This tragic scenario is happening to children all over the world in every war.

title: The Opposite Jars: Posi and Nega
awards: Best Short Story — Catholic Mass Media Awards (2017)
blurb: The opposite jars are always having an argument because Posi has a very cheerful outlook about life while Nega think that every situation will always turn out for the worst. Until the time came when both of them were kept inside a dark and dusty room. This story will help children understand that a negative experience is not a reason for them to give up on life and every obstacle can be resolved with a positive attitude.

title: The Smelly Fruit
awards: 2nd Place — AFCC Samsung KidsTime Author's Award, Singapore (2016)
blurb: According to the legend, Durian had all the qualities a fruit could ever wish for. It was known as the perfect fruit. The King of Fruits as often called was respected and admired by everyone. This made Durian arrogant criticizing all the other fruits in the island.
note: Filipino title: Ang Mabahong Prutas (updated Book Titles.docx lists the English title)

title: Why Is A Pig's Nose Flat?
awards: 2nd Place — AFCC Samsung KidsTime Author's Award, Singapore (2016)
blurb: Long ago, all the animals did not have noses. One day their wish was granted. But the pig did not believe the good news. What will happen when the pig is the only one left with just two holes on his face?

title: EL and EY: The Adventurous Shells
awards: 2nd Place — AFCC Samsung KidsTime Author's Award, Singapore (2016)
blurb: El and Ey are seashells curious about the real meaning of love. They asked the King of the Sea but they were not satisfied with his answers so they had decided to go to the seashore and find out for themselves. On their way, they experienced hardships and dangers. They were separated. They were about to give up when something happened during their exciting adventures that made them realized valuable lesson about loving others. How children that they don’t have to be alone in coping with their emotional difficulties.

title: The Little Seed
awards: 2nd Place — AFCC Samsung KidsTime Author's Award, Singapore (2016)
blurb: The Little Seed is a beautiful story about kindness and love. The children will learn that respect is not given because of wealth but because of the goodness one shares with others.

title: Diola: Heroine of Philippine Eagles
awards: 2nd Place — AFCC Samsung KidsTime Author's Award, Singapore (2016)
blurb: Our national bird, the Philippine eagle, is known as the largest and most extraordinary bird in the country. But do you know that Diola, the mother of Pag-asa and Pagkakaisa, demonstrated the scientific phenomenon that eagles fall in love with human beings? Through her, the Philippines became the first country in the world to successfully hatch an egg from an eagle using artificial means.

title: A Crumpled Piece of Paper
blurb: Fermin finds a ball of paper under a Talisay tree. Written on the paper is a poem about loving one’s home and ways to show that love. Fermin shares this poem to his father, his friends, until they discover the poem’s author ... Dr. Jose Rizal! This is a fictional reimagining of how Rizal’s poem “Hymn to Talisay” inspired the people around him. This story will help inspire children to make their community a better place, no matter their age.

title: A Mother's Love in Every Hop
blurb: The little kangaroo grew strong under the loving care of his mother. She carried him in her pouch, kept him safe, and taught him everything he needed to know. But one day, it was time for him to hop out into the world on his own. With courage in his heart and the lessons of home in his mind, he left to explore the beautiful world, ready for new adventures while carrying his mother’s love with him.

title: Amihan's Colorful Coconut Leaf Slippers
blurb: Sometimes, the most precious things are the ones made with love. Amihan’s slippers are not fancy or expensive. They are woven from coconut leaves by her Papa, with a tiny heart on the straps to remind her how much he loves her.

title: Balloons Fly, Animals Cry
blurb: We watch balloons float beautifully, never thinking about where they land. Have you ever wondered where balloons go when they fly away? This wordless book invites children to look beyond the sky and discover how small choices can make a big difference for nature.

title: Be Yourself, Be Brave
blurb: Twin siblings Mara and Marlon discover that boys and girls can do anything they dream of. By following their hearts and being brave, they learn that the best way to shine is to be themselves and do what they love.

title: Don't Touch The Starfish
blurb: When Little Starfish is left alone on the beach after a storm, she is found by Nathalie and Marco. They play with her and want to take her home and put her in a giant fishbowl. But Little Starfish is more than just a pet. This story teaches children that loving animals is much more than just keeping them as pets.

title: Learning About The Philippines: Counting Book
blurb: The famous wonders of the Philippines are more than just beautiful places. They show us the amazing wonders of nature and the creativity of our Filipino ancestors. By learning about these wonders, children will understand the importance of protecting our environment, appreciate Filipino traditions, and value of our culture and heritage.

title: Mga Kilalang Yaman ng Pilipinas
blurb: The Philippines is home to many amazing natural and cultural wonders. Children can explore these beautiful places and rich traditions through a fun and exciting comic book.

title: Memories of Agila
blurb: Paul and his father loved making kites and flying them together. One day, Paul’s father made him an eagle-shaped kite before he left to work overseas. Paul loses the kite. How did he learn a valuable lesson on loss and acceptance.

title: Mother Turtle's Nest
blurb: From Tiny to Mighty - The Science of Life Cycles (Turtles) Every living thing grows and changes through a life cycle. In this series, children explore how plants, animals, and humans are born, grow, and live-discovering the amazing journey from tiny beginnings to mighty life.

title: My Father, The Honest Mayor
blurb: A boy narrates the good things his father has done as a town mayor. He admires and looks up at him as a good man and a hero. This story will teach children that every community has the chance to grow and improve if elected leaders are honest and sincere to do what is right in fulfilling the needs of the people.

title: Purple Hands, Loving Hands
blurb: For Phebie, purple once meant joy, family, and the sweet taste of ube. After Grandma’s accident, it feels different-until Grandma shows her that love can turn even painful moments into something beautiful again. A story of love, resilience, and the color purple that holds them together.

title: Si Karla Feeling Prinsesa
blurb: Sanay si Karla na alagaan siya na parang prinsesa... hanggang isang umaga, kailangan niyang gawin ang lahat mag-isa! Matutuklasan kaya niya na kaya pala niyang alagaan ang sarili?

title: The Flood Took Lyka Away
blurb: Mila lost her favorite doll Lyka in the flood. She was given another doll, but Mila still missed Lyka. Over time, Mila learns to deal with her grief and cherish the memories she has of her lost doll. This story teaches children on dealing with loss and cherishing happy memories.

title: The Log of Hope
blurb: A once-forgotten log lay abandoned in the forest, feeling small and useless. But when a great flood came, it became a light of hope and courage. From a simple log to a family’s greatest treasure, this is a heartwarming story of love, resilience, and the power to rise above every storm.

title: A Basket In War
blurb: When there is a war, children often rely on their families for protection. This is a different story. A basket kept one child safe from war. A basket gave him hope and faith. A basket gave him the inspiration to help children affected by war.

title: A Great Miracle
blurb: In this story, we will feel the woman's faith upon God as she tried to do something valuable, lasting and meaningful by sewing three fabrics. The first fabric wrapped a most precious gift on earth. The second fabric was worn by the greatest master, and the third fabric showed the image of the son of God. Til the day the woman was afflicted with illness, she never knew that the cloth she has sewn and touched were her great offerings to God.

title: Ako Ay Pilipino: Mahahalagang Kaugaliang Pilipino
blurb: Comics are a wonderful graphic medium for telling stories to children. They can more easily understand the message and meaning of what they read because the images speak and bring the story to life. The stories in comics are also connected to everyday events and happenings in our lives and in the world. For the very first time, we wholeheartedly present to young readers the KIDZKOMIKZ series - important Filipino Values for Children.

title: Bakit Malinis ang Ngipin ng Buwaya?
blurb: One day, news spread through the jungle-the chickens had lost their teeth! Crocodile got worried. What if he lost his teeth too? So, he set off to visit his animal friends and ask how they keep their teeth clean and strong. This light-hearted story teaches children the importance of taking care of their teeth and shows how different animals do it in their own special ways.

title: Bakit Walang Ngipin Ang Mga Manok?
blurb: Long ago, when chickens still had teeth, they chewed and bit almost everything in sight. They never cared for their teeth because they were strong and sharp. But what could have happened that made them lose their teeth? A delightful and amusing story that teaches children the importance of avoiding too many sweets that can cause tooth decay.

title: Chatkak The Talkative Frog
note: Not in Book Titles.docx list — confirm with client No blurb or Shopee link — this title has no row in the client's Aug 2026 spreadsheet.

title: Cindy's 365 Bags and More
blurb: Cindy’s room was filled with bags. She would dream of an island full of bags. All the people, trees, flowers, stars and the moon were bags. Until one day, something happened. A giant wall of bags blocked her door. Read this story and find out the mystery of Cindy’s 365 bags!

title: Crossing The Red Sea
blurb: The Old Testament contains many of the earliest and most meaningful stories in the Bible. This series introduces these timeless stories to children in a simple and engaging way, helping them understand important lessons about faith, courage, and obedience. Filled with wonder, adventure, and beautiful full-color illustrations, these retold stories make learning about the Bible enjoyable and meaningful for young readers.

title: Daniel In The Lion's Den
blurb: The Old Testament contains many of the earliest and most meaningful stories in the Bible. This series introduces these timeless stories to children in a simple and engaging way, helping them understand important lessons about faith, courage, and obedience. Filled with wonder, adventure, and beautiful full-color illustrations, these retold stories make learning about the Bible enjoyable and meaningful for young readers.

title: Dessert Town Is Melting!
blurb: For Little David, Dessert Town is the coolest place. It has unlimited ice cream and other desserts as long as you don’t eat too much of it. But then Mr. Gobbler arrives and decides to eat more than what is good for anyone... Dessert town is like Mother Earth that provides us with many precious gifts like clean air, forests, water, shelter and food to live. If we take too much, we lose the gifts. We destroy our home, we destroy our lives.

title: Don't Take My Colors Away!
blurb: Fuzz, is a huge butterfly who would scrape off and steal the colors of the little butterflies until their wings become so ugly. He warned them not to tell anyone. How can the little butterflies get back their colors? This book aims to help parents discuss important conversations with children about boundaries, what is appropriate, and how to stay safe from being harmed. A story for those who care.

title: Fluffy's Misadventure Week! It's All Gone
blurb: Do you need your child to practice the sequencing of the days of the week while having fun? Do you need your child to practice saying how they feel?This is the right book for you. A story that introduces the mischievous adventures of fluffy and her family as she goes through the days of the week.

title: Flying Trash
blurb: Trash is everywhere, thrown from cars, buses, and by careless hands on the streets. But one day, the roads had enough. Bumps and hills grew taller, making the roads “sick.” They hatched a clever plan to rid themselves of all the litter, and it surprised the whole city! A fun and imaginative story that teaches children the importance of taking care of the environment.

title: Grandma's Baked Goodies
blurb: Grandma is ready for Gianne’s visit. For Gianne, Grandma has already prepared cupcakes and cookies of different amounts and sizes that fill both the tummy and the heart. A book that encourages counting and critical thinking as children analyze the mathematical concepts presented in the story. They will also learn the Immense value of loving and caring for family members.

title: Home Is Where The Heart Lives
blurb: Areana lost her home many times but instead of giving up, she chose to stand up to those trials with courage, perseverance and dignity. Her ability to adapt to a tough situation was so strong. She kept on building a new home and did not waste her time complaining. She continued to live with hope even in the most difficult circumstances. A beautiful story for children about making choices in responding to tragic situations and uncertainties that will allow them to hope for a better future.

title: Jesus Feeds 5000 People
blurb: The Bible is a very old book but it is very important for children to know about Bible. So, in the present series “New Testament” Bible stories are retold to help the children understand the bible better. These stories have adventure, mystery and rules in an interesting way with exquisite colorful illustrations. Young readers will definitely enjoy these exciting stories.

title: May Aswang Sa Iskul?
blurb: Wherever we are faced with a new environment or situation, we become anxious, fearful, and doubtful. This is how children feel whenever they are left in school. Because of fear, many thoughts ran through his imagination which heightened his suspicion. What will happen to him if he thinks that his teacher is a witch who would, at any time, hurt or eat him?

title: Meaningful Values For God's Children
blurb: Teachers have a great responsibility to help their students become not just good people but also great human beings. Through this book, Meaningful Values for God's Children, we teach them the right set of values and social skills.

title: Mom's Best Playdough Activities: Bread & Pastries
blurb: These playdough activity book is perfect for kids and kids at heart. With adorable clay art and easy-to-follow instructions, it brings a whole lot of wonder and fun in creating with clay. Featuring engaging projects that kids can enjoy, it will amaze you and your little ones as to what you can make with clay.

title: My Muslim Friend
blurb: This is a true story of a touching friendship between Muslim and a Christian girl in Mindanao. They were the best of friends since childhood. They sincerely cared for the well-being of each other. They proved that both culture could be together in peace and unity because they respected their differences in ethnicity and religion . They valued their friendship more than the opinion of other’s beliefs and ideologies in this world.

title: My Pink Spot
blurb: Anything that is different is perceived as ugly in this world. People are treated as if there is something wrong or missing. Our society feeds false messages to children about what is to be valued. With Ana, the spot on her face was not a hindrance to make her feel happy and beautiful. A birthmark that is usually a cause for humiliation becomes a source of pride --- a beauty spot!

title: The Hairy Fruit
blurb: Have you seen three sisters with long colorful hair and a bald brother attached to each other? That is how the legend of the Rambutan fruit started. These four children were known to be strange because of their appearance, and unusual because of their attitude. One day, they passed by the Island of Fruits. Find out the harm they did to the fruits and how the learned the value of loving one another.

title: The Kingdom With No Stories
blurb: Long ago, there lived a king who hated stories. He believes that writing and reading stories will not help his kingdom to prosper. But there was a humble lady named Rainmari who could not accept this rule. She secretly wrote her stories at night and kept it inside her huge rag dol. What will happen when the king learns about her secret?

title: Tuna Festival
blurb: Every September, General Santos City, the Tuna Capital of the Philippines, celebrates the Tuna Festival. Discover the sights, sounds, smells, and taste that the magical event has to offer. Who know? Maybe it’s a place you’d like to visit this coming September!

title: Two Hats, One Heart
blurb: “Olivia and Anna are different in many ways, but just like their hats, they are the same at heart. They share what truly matters. They both believe in kindness and lasting friendships. A story that highlights understanding, respect, and shared values between a Muslim and a Christian girl.”

title: Where Shall We Build Our Nest?
blurb: Above the city with barely any trees, Mama Bird and Papa Bird gasp for air. They’ve been flying for days, looking for a safe place to build a nest. Time is running short. Without any trees to build a nest on, how will Mama Bird lay her eggs?
